faq.a2: Only images are extracted. Text and vector drawings (lines, tables, many logos) aren’t images; to keep them, use PDF to JPG, which converts the whole page.
faq.q3: What about a scanned PDF?
faq.a3: Each scanned page is an image, so you’ll get one image per page at the scan’s resolution.
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

markdown-to-pdf.title: Markdown to PDF
markdown-to-pdf.description: Turn Markdown (with tables, task lists and code) into a well laid out PDF, in A4 or Letter.
markdown-to-pdf.about: Markdown to PDF turns your notes, READMEs or documentation written in Markdown into a PDF ready to print or send. It supports GitHub flavor: tables, strikethrough, task lists and code blocks. Headings, lists and tables are laid out with readable margins and type, and links keep working inside the PDF.

faq.q1: Which Markdown elements are kept?
faq.a1: Headings, bold, italics, lists (including task lists), tables, quotes, code blocks, links and horizontal rules, in GitHub flavor (GFM). The PDF title is the first level-1 heading.
faq.q2: Are images included?
faq.a2: Only those embedded in the Markdown itself as data URLs (data:image/png;base64,…). Images linked from the web or from files on your computer are not downloaded: their alt text is shown instead. That way the server never reaches external addresses.
faq.q3: What happens to HTML written inside the Markdown?
faq.a3: For safety only its text is kept: tags, scripts, styles and iframes are removed before the PDF is made.
faq.q4: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: Yes: the PDF is made on our own server (not a third-party service), over an encrypted connection, and the file is processed in memory without being stored. If you'd rather nothing leaves your device, use Markdown to HTML and print the page as PDF from your browser.

html-to-pdf.title: HTML to PDF
html-to-pdf.description: Turn an HTML file into a PDF that keeps its styles, tables and embedded images, in A4 or Letter.
html-to-pdf.about: HTML to PDF prints saved web pages, email templates, invoices or exported reports as a PDF ready to send. Styles written inside the file (style tags and attributes), tables and images embedded as data URLs are kept. If the HTML sets its own page size with @page, that size is used.

faq.q1: Can I convert a web page from its address (URL)?
faq.a1: No: you upload or paste the HTML file. For safety our server never visits internet or internal addresses while making the PDF.
faq.q2: Why are some images or styles missing?
faq.a2: Only what is inside the file is used: styles in style tags or attributes, and images embedded as data URLs. Linked stylesheets, fonts and images (link, src or url() pointing to another file or site) are not downloaded.
faq.q3: Does the page's JavaScript run?
faq.a3: No. Scripts, event attributes, iframes, objects and redirects are removed before printing; you get what the page shows without JavaScript. Pages that build their content with JavaScript will come out incomplete.
faq.q4: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: Yes: the PDF is made on our own server (not a third-party service), over an encrypted connection, and the file is processed in memory without being stored.

pdf-to-pdfa.title: PDF to PDF/A
pdf-to-pdfa.description: Convert a PDF to the PDF/A archival format (1b, 2b or 3b) for long-term storage or official submissions.
pdf-to-pdfa.about: PDF to PDF/A turns your PDFs into the long-term archival format required by many public agencies, courts and universities. PDF/A embeds every font, pins colors to a profile and stores the metadata inside the file, so the document looks the same many years from now. The result is checked with the veraPDF reference validator.

faq.q1: Which PDF/A version should I choose?
faq.a1: Unless you are asked for another, PDF/A-2b: it is the most widely accepted and supports transparency and modern compression. PDF/A-1b is for older systems that only accept the first version; PDF/A-3b also allows files attached inside the PDF (e-invoices, for example).
faq.q2: Does the document's appearance change?
faq.a2: Content and pages stay the same. Some details may vary: fonts are embedded and, in PDF/A-1b, transparency is flattened. Links and interactive forms may be lost because the archival format does not allow them.
faq.q3: Can I convert a password-protected PDF?
faq.a3: No: PDF/A does not allow encryption. Remove the password first with “Remove a PDF password” and then convert it.
faq.q4: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: Yes: the conversion runs on our own server (not a third-party service), over an encrypted connection, and the file is processed in memory without being stored.

pdf-to-excel.title: PDF to Excel
pdf-to-excel.description: Extract the tables of a PDF to Excel (XLSX) or CSV in your browser, with a preview and real numbers, without uploading the file.
pdf-to-excel.about: Turn the tables of a bank statement, a price list, an invoice or a report in PDF into a spreadsheet. The tool reads the PDF's text with its position on the page, builds rows from the line each text sits on and columns from how they line up, and shows you the detected table before you download. Amounts such as 1,234.56 or 1.234,56 become real numbers you can add up, and codes with leading zeros stay as text. Get one sheet per page, one per table or everything in a single sheet. It works with PDFs that contain text (the ones a program creates); a scanned PDF is an image and needs text recognition (OCR) first.

faq.q1: Which PDFs does it work with?
faq.a1: Those with selectable text: the ones a bank, an invoicing system, Word or Excel create with “Save as PDF”. If you can select a word with the mouse when you open the PDF, it will work. A scan or a photo turned into a PDF has no text: run it through “OCR scanned PDF” first and use the PDF it gives you back, knowing that accuracy will be lower.
faq.q2: Why isn't the table perfect?
faq.a2: A PDF does not store tables, only pieces of text and their positions, so columns are worked out from the alignment. Cells with text on several lines may come out as separate rows, and a cell spanning two columns may land in one. Check the preview before downloading; if numbers come out as text, pick the decimal separator yourself.
faq.q3: How are numbers with a decimal comma recognized?
faq.a3: Per table: if amounts are written like 84.35 or 1,234.56, the point is the decimal separator; if they are written like 84,35 or 1.234,56, it is the comma. A space as thousands separator (1 250,5) is recognized too. Dates, percentages and amounts with a currency symbol stay as text, as they appear.
faq.a4: No. The PDF is read in your browser with pdf.js and the spreadsheet is built on your device with SheetJS: nothing is sent to any server. PDFs of up to 100 MB are accepted.

spreadsheet-converter.title: Spreadsheet converter
spreadsheet-converter.description: Convert between Excel (XLSX, XLS), OpenDocument (ODS) and CSV: every sheet, value and formula, in your browser.
spreadsheet-converter.about: Convert spreadsheets between Excel (XLSX and the older XLS), OpenDocument (ODS, from LibreOffice) and CSV or TSV. Turn a CSV exported by some system into an Excel file ready to work with, or an Excel file into CSV to load into another app. When reading a CSV the separator is detected and numbers with a decimal comma are recognized; when writing one you can choose comma or semicolon so that Excel in other languages opens it correctly.

faq.q1: What is kept?
faq.a1: Every sheet, the values (text, numbers, dates) and formulas with their last result. Visual formatting is not kept: colors, fonts, borders, column widths, charts and images.
faq.q2: Why does Excel show broken accents or everything in one column?
faq.a2: Excel in many European and Latin American languages expects a semicolon separator and a decimal comma. Choose “Semicolon” and keep UTF-8 with BOM checked so accented letters display correctly on double-click.
faq.q3: What happens to a workbook with several sheets when converting to CSV?
faq.a3: A CSV holds one table, so one CSV is made per sheet (with the sheet name in the file name), or only the first sheet's if you uncheck the option.
faq.a4: Up to 50 MB per file and 2 million filled cells, because everything is processed in your browser's memory. Your files are not uploaded to any server.

excel-to-csv.title: Excel to CSV
excel-to-csv.description: Convert an Excel file (XLSX, XLS or ODS) to CSV in your browser: pick the sheet, the separator and UTF-8 with BOM so accents show correctly.
excel-to-csv.about: Turn an Excel sheet into CSV to load it into another system, a database or an online spreadsheet. If the workbook has several sheets, pick the one to convert or get one CSV per sheet. Numbers keep every decimal (not rounded the way they look on screen), dates come out as Excel shows them and codes with leading zeros, such as 007, are kept. Choose comma, semicolon (with decimal comma, as Excel uses in many European and Latin American languages) or tab.

faq.q1: Which separator should I choose?
faq.a1: Comma if the CSV goes to another program or system (it is the standard). Semicolon if you will open it with Excel set to a language that writes decimals with a comma, such as Spanish, Portuguese, French or German: each value then lands in its own column. Tab if the system asks for TSV.
faq.q2: Why do accents look wrong when I open the CSV in Excel?
faq.a2: Excel on Windows does not recognize UTF-8 unless the file says so. Keep “UTF-8 with BOM” checked: it adds an invisible mark at the start and Excel shows accents and other alphabets correctly.
faq.q3: My workbook has several sheets. What happens?
faq.a3: A CSV holds a single table. With one workbook you pick the sheet from the list, or “All sheets”, which creates one CSV per sheet named after it. With several workbooks at once, the first sheet of each is used unless you check the all-sheets option.
faq.a4: No. The conversion runs in your browser with SheetJS; the file never leaves your device. Files of up to 50 MB and 2 million filled cells are accepted.

csv-to-excel.title: CSV to Excel
csv-to-excel.description: Convert a CSV or TSV file to Excel (XLSX) in your browser, with correct numbers and accents even if it uses semicolons or Windows-1252.
csv-to-excel.about: Open as Excel the CSV exported by a bank, an online store or an invoicing system. The separator (comma, semicolon, tab or pipe) and the encoding are detected, including the Windows-1252 encoding that CSV files saved by Excel on Windows often use. Numbers with a decimal comma in a semicolon CSV become real numbers, and codes with leading zeros, such as 007, stay as text so they are not lost.

faq.q1: Why not just open the CSV with Excel?
faq.a1: Excel often puts everything in one column when the separator does not match your settings, shows accents wrongly if the file is UTF-8 without a BOM, and drops the leading zeros of codes and phone numbers. Converted here, the XLSX has every value in its own cell.
faq.q2: How are numbers recognized?
faq.a2: A value becomes a number only if it reads back the same: 3.25 or, in a semicolon CSV, 3,25 and 1.234,5. Codes like 007 and integers longer than 15 digits (such as card or bank account numbers) stay as text so Excel does not round them.
faq.q3: What about dates?
faq.a3: They are kept as they appear in the CSV, as text. Excel can convert them with Data → Text to Columns if you need real dates for calculations.
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser; the CSV never leaves your device. You can convert several at once, up to 50 MB each.

xls-to-xlsx.title: XLS to XLSX
xls-to-xlsx.description: Convert old Excel spreadsheets (XLS, Excel 97-2003) to the current XLSX format in your browser, with every sheet and formula.
xls-to-xlsx.about: XLS is the Excel 97-2003 format. Many systems, forms and online apps only accept XLSX now, which is also smaller. This tool copies every sheet, value and formula of the XLS into a new XLSX, without installing anything or uploading the file.

faq.q1: What is kept?
faq.a1: Every sheet with its name, the values (text, numbers, dates) and the formulas. Visual formatting is not kept: colors, borders, column widths, charts and macros.
faq.q2: Why convert XLS to XLSX?
faq.a2: XLSX has been Excel's default format since Excel 2007: Excel, LibreOffice, Google Sheets and Numbers open it, it allows more rows (over a million instead of 65,536) and it is usually smaller because it is compressed.
faq.q3: Does it work with password-protected files?
faq.a3: No. An encrypted XLS cannot be read without its password; open it in Excel, remove the protection and try again.
faq.a4: No. The conversion happens in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

excel-to-ods.title: Excel to ODS
excel-to-ods.description: Convert Excel (XLSX or XLS) to ODS, the LibreOffice Calc format that some public bodies ask for, in your browser.
excel-to-ods.about: ODS (OpenDocument) is the open format of LibreOffice and OpenOffice, and the one some public bodies require. This tool turns the sheets, values and formulas of an Excel file into a valid ODS without installing LibreOffice and without uploading the file to any server.

faq.q1: Are formulas kept?
faq.a1: Yes. Formulas are written in OpenDocument syntax, so LibreOffice recalculates them when it opens the file. Visual formatting (colors, borders, widths) is not kept.
faq.q2: Can I open the ODS in Excel?
faq.a2: Yes, Excel opens ODS files, and so do Google Sheets and LibreOffice.
faq.q3: What about charts and macros?
faq.a3: They are not copied: the data and formulas are converted. If you need the charts, save the file as ODS from Excel or LibreOffice.
faq.a4: No. Everything is processed in your browser.

ods-to-excel.title: ODS to Excel
ods-to-excel.description: Convert LibreOffice or OpenOffice spreadsheets (ODS) to Excel (XLSX) in your browser, with every sheet and formula.
ods-to-excel.about: If someone sent you an .ods spreadsheet (LibreOffice Calc, OpenOffice) and you need to hand it in as Excel, convert it to XLSX here in seconds. Every sheet, value and formula is kept, and the file never leaves your device.

faq.q1: What is kept?
faq.a1: The sheets with their names, the values (text, numbers, dates) and the formulas. Visual formatting is not kept: colors, borders, widths, charts and images.
faq.q2: Do formulas still work in Excel?
faq.a2: Yes, the usual formulas (sums, averages, conditions, lookups and arithmetic) are written in Excel syntax. A function that only exists in LibreOffice may show an error in Excel.
faq.q3: Can I convert several files at once?
faq.a3: Yes. Pick them together and download them one by one or all in a ZIP.
faq.a4: No. The conversion runs in your browser.

excel-to-json.title: Excel to JSON
excel-to-json.description: Convert an Excel sheet (XLSX, XLS or ODS) to JSON in your browser: each row as an object keyed by the headers.
excel-to-json.about: Turn a spreadsheet into JSON to use it in an app, an API or a script. The first row is taken as the header and every following row becomes an object with those keys; you can also get the rows as lists. Numbers stay numbers, TRUE/FALSE cells become true/false, dates use ISO format (2024-03-15) and empty cells become null. With a multi-sheet workbook, pick one sheet or get them all in a single object.

faq.q1: What does the JSON look like?
faq.a1: With “Objects” you get a list like ['{'"product": "Coffee", "price": 3.25'}', …], using the first row as keys. With “Lists” you get every row as a list of values, the first one included. If you choose all sheets, the result is an object with one list per sheet.
faq.q2: How do dates come out?
faq.a2: As ISO 8601 text: 2024-03-15, or 2024-03-15T10:30:00 when they have a time. It is the format JavaScript, Python and databases understand.
faq.q3: What about empty or repeated headers?
faq.a3: An empty header is named after its column, such as column3, and a repeated one gets a suffix, such as name_2, so no column is lost.
faq.a4: No. The conversion runs in your browser; the file never leaves your device.

json-to-excel.title: JSON to Excel
json-to-excel.description: Convert JSON (a list of objects or of lists) to Excel (XLSX) in your browser, with one column per key and real dates and numbers.
json-to-excel.about: Open in Excel the data an API or an app exported as JSON. A list of objects becomes a table with one column per key (in order of appearance) and one row per object; a list of lists is copied as is. If the JSON is an object whose values are lists, each one goes to its own sheet. Numbers and true/false stay as such, ISO dates (2024-03-15) become Excel dates and nested values are stored as JSON text.

faq.q1: Which JSON is accepted?
faq.a1: A list of objects (['{'"a": 1'}', '{'"a": 2'}']), a list of lists ([["a", "b"], [1, 2]]), a list of values, a single object (one row) or an object with several lists, such as '{'"customers": [...], "sales": [...]'}', which gives one sheet per list.
faq.q2: What if the objects do not all have the same keys?
faq.a2: A column is created for every key found in any object; where an object lacks it, the cell is left empty.
faq.q3: What about nested objects or lists?
faq.a3: A cell holds a single value, so nested data is written as JSON text (for example ["a","b"]). To flatten it into columns, use “JSON to CSV”, which names them like address.city.
faq.a4: No. Everything is processed in your browser. Files of up to 50 MB are accepted.

merge-excel.title: Merge Excel files
merge-excel.description: Combine several Excel, ODS or CSV files into one workbook, with a sheet per file or every row in a single sheet, in your browser.
merge-excel.about: Put the Excel files of several months, branches or people into a single file. Make every sheet of every file a sheet of the new workbook (a CSV or a one-sheet file takes the file's name), or stack all the rows in one sheet, one below the other, to filter and add them up together. When stacking, the header repeated at the top of each sheet is kept only once and, if you want, a first column tells which file each row comes from. Order the files before merging: they are used in that order.

faq.q1: What is the difference between the two ways of merging?
faq.a1: “One sheet per sheet” copies the sheets as they are into a new workbook, with their formulas. “All in one sheet” puts the rows of every sheet one under another: use it when they all have the same columns, such as each month's sales.
faq.q2: Are formulas kept?
faq.a2: When each sheet stays a sheet, yes. When stacking, no, because rows move and formulas would point at other cells: each formula's result is kept as a value.
faq.q3: Can I merge the sheets of a single file?
faq.a3: Yes: pick one workbook and “All in one sheet” to stack all its sheets into one.
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser with SheetJS; the files never leave your device. Visual formatting (colors, borders, widths) is not kept.

split-excel.title: Split Excel sheets
split-excel.description: Split every sheet of an Excel or ODS workbook into its own file (XLSX, ODS or CSV) and download them all in a ZIP, in your browser.
split-excel.about: When a workbook has one sheet per month, customer or branch and you need to send each one separately, this tool creates one file per sheet named after it, ready to download one by one or all together in a ZIP. Get them as Excel (XLSX), OpenDocument (ODS) or CSV. Formulas inside each sheet are kept; those that use data from another sheet are replaced by their result, because that other sheet will not be in the file.

faq.q1: What are the files called?
faq.a1: After the workbook and the sheet, for example sales-January.xlsx. Characters that are not allowed in file names are replaced with an underscore.
faq.q2: What happens to formulas that use other sheets?
faq.a2: A formula like =Summary!B2 would stop working in a file with a single sheet, so its last result is kept as a value. Other formulas stay formulas.
faq.q3: Can I split several workbooks at once?
faq.a3: Yes. Pick several files and each one is split into its sheets; everything can be downloaded in a ZIP.
faq.a4: No. The workbook is processed in your browser and never leaves your device.

create-archive.title: Create ZIP
create-archive.description: Put several files in one ZIP, TAR or TAR.GZ in your browser, without uploading them to any server.
create-archive.about: Bundle several files into one to email them, upload them to a form or keep them together. Choose ZIP, the format Windows, macOS, Android and iPhone open without installing anything, or TAR and TAR.GZ, the usual ones on Linux and servers. You can choose how much to compress: photos, videos and Office documents are already compressed and are stored as they are, so no time is wasted; text, PDF and other files do get smaller.

faq.q1: Which format should I pick: ZIP, TAR or TAR.GZ?
faq.a1: ZIP if you're sending it to other people: any computer or phone opens it. TAR.GZ is the standard on Linux and for uploading files to a server. TAR only bundles the files without compressing them.
faq.q2: Why is the ZIP almost as big as my files?
faq.a2: Photos (JPG, PNG, WEBP), videos, audio and Office documents are already compressed inside, so compressing them again doesn't make them smaller. To make photos lighter, use “Compress image” before creating the ZIP.
faq.q3: Are names with accents or Chinese characters kept?
faq.a3: Yes. Names are stored in UTF-8, as current programs expect. If two files have the same name, the second becomes “name (1)”. Slashes in names are replaced so nothing can be written outside the folder when extracting.
faq.q4: Is there a size limit? Can I add a password?
faq.a4: Everything is built in your browser's memory, so the files can add up to 500 MB in total. Password-protected ZIPs aren't available yet: to protect a document, use “Password protect a PDF”.

extract-archive.title: Extract ZIP
extract-archive.description: Open ZIP, RAR, 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ and GZ files in your browser and download what's inside, with its folders.
extract-archive.about: Open an archive without installing any program: handy on a phone, a work computer or a tablet. You see the list of files it holds and can download each one separately or all together in a ZIP with the same folders. Works with ZIP (including ones made by older Windows versions, with accented names), RAR (versions 4 and 5), 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ/TGZ and GZ. The archive is opened on your device: it isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Is it safe to open a ZIP someone sent me?
faq.a1: It is opened as a potentially hostile file: nothing is run, paths that try to leave the folder (like “../”) are fixed, symbolic links and special files are skipped, and “zip bombs” stop once they pass the limit. Still, scan programs downloaded from unknown sources with an antivirus.
faq.q2: Which formats can it open?
faq.a2: ZIP, RAR (4 and 5), 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ (or TGZ) and GZ. Password-protected archives can't be opened here yet, nor ZIPs using unusual compression methods or RARs split into parts.
faq.q3: Is there a limit?
faq.a3: The archive can be up to 500 MB (RAR and 7Z up to 250 MB), and its contents up to 500 MB and 5,000 files in total, because everything is extracted in your browser's memory.
faq.a4: Yes: each file shows its path, and downloading everything together creates a ZIP with the same folder structure. Empty folders are not included.

image-to-text.title: Image to text (OCR)
image-to-text.description: Extract text from photos, screenshots and scanned documents with OCR, in your browser, without uploading the images.
image-to-text.about: Turn the text in an image into editable text: a photo of a document, a screenshot, a receipt or a scanned page. Choose the language of the text (Spanish, English, Portuguese, French or Chinese) for more accurate recognition. Everything happens on your device: the OCR engine and the language are downloaded once from our site and your images are not uploaded to any server. You get one .txt file per image, which you can also copy directly.

faq.q1: How accurate is it?
faq.a1: With sharp, straight printed text it usually gets almost everything right. Blurry, tilted or dark photos and handwriting give worse results; when confidence is low we warn you to check the text.
faq.q2: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a2: No. Recognition runs in your browser. Only the OCR engine and the chosen language model (about 2 to 4 MB) are downloaded the first time, from our own site.
faq.q3: Which formats and languages are supported?
faq.a3: JPG, PNG, WEBP, BMP, GIF, TIFF, HEIC and AVIF, up to 50 MB per image. Languages: Spanish, English, Portuguese, French and Simplified Chinese. Choose the language the text is written in.
faq.q4: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
faq.a4: If your PDF is a scan, use “OCR scanned PDF”: it recognizes every page and gives you a searchable PDF or a .txt file.

ocr-pdf.title: OCR scanned PDF
ocr-pdf.description: Turn a scanned PDF into a PDF with text you can search and copy, or extract its text, in your browser.
ocr-pdf.about: A scanned PDF is just a picture of each page: you can't search for a word or copy the text. This tool recognizes the text of each page with OCR and adds it as an invisible layer over the original page, which doesn't change: the PDF looks the same, but now you can search, select and copy. You can also get only the text as a .txt file. Pages that already have digital text are left as they are. Everything is processed on your device.

faq.q1: Does the PDF look different?
faq.a1: No. The original pages are kept as they are (same quality, same size); the recognized text is added on top, invisible, in the same position as the words in the image.
faq.q2: How many pages can it process?
faq.a2: Up to 100 pages and 100 MB per PDF. Each page is recognized in your browser and takes a few seconds, so a long document can take several minutes.
faq.q3: What about pages that already have text?
faq.a3: With the option checked they are left as they are, and their text goes into the .txt unchanged. Uncheck it if a page has only a little digital text (a stamp, for example) besides the scan.
faq.q4: Are my documents uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: No. The PDF is opened, read and recognized in your browser; only the OCR engine and the language model are downloaded once from our site.

epub-converter.title: EPUB Converter
epub-converter.description: Convert EPUB books into one HTML page or plain text (TXT), with images and a table of contents. In your browser.
epub-converter.about: Turn an EPUB ebook into a single HTML file that opens in any browser, with the cover, a table of contents, the chapters in order and the images included, or into plain text (.txt) to read it on any device, search it or copy from it. Works with DRM-free EPUB 2 and EPUB 3 books. Links between chapters keep working inside the page. The book is opened on your device: it isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Does it work with books bought with DRM?
faq.a1: No. EPUBs protected with DRM (Adobe, Readium LCP, Apple) are encrypted and can only be read in the store's app; the tool tells you so. DRM-free EPUBs work: public domain books, books from DRM-free publishers or ones you made.
faq.q2: Is the HTML it makes safe?
faq.a2: Yes. Scripts, event handlers, forms and javascript: links are removed, and the page carries a security policy that blocks loading anything from the internet: images are stored inside the file. The book's stylesheets aren't used; the page has its own reading styles, light and dark.
faq.q3: What is lost in the conversion?
faq.a3: The book's styles (fonts, colors, margins), audio, video and external images. Plain text keeps paragraphs, headings, lists (with dashes) and tables (cells separated by tabs).
faq.a4: Up to 100 MB per book and 300 MB unpacked, because everything is processed in your browser's memory. You can convert several books at once and download them in a ZIP.

epub-to-pdf.title: EPUB to PDF
epub-to-pdf.description: Convert EPUB books into PDFs ready to print or read on any device, with a table of contents and images.
epub-to-pdf.about: Turn an EPUB ebook into a PDF with the cover, a table of contents, each chapter starting on a new page and the images included, in A4 or Letter size. Handy to print a book, read it on a device that can't open EPUB or share it with someone without an ebook reader. Works with DRM-free EPUB 2 and EPUB 3 books. The book is opened in your browser and only the assembled page (without scripts) is sent to our server to print it; it's deleted when done.

faq.q1: Does it work with books bought with DRM?
faq.a1: No. EPUBs protected with DRM (Adobe, Readium LCP, Apple) are encrypted and can't be read outside the store's app; the tool tells you before sending anything.
faq.q2: Is the book's layout kept?
faq.a2: Text, headings, lists, tables, images and links between chapters are kept, with a reading layout of our own: each chapter starts on a new page. The book's fonts, colors and margins are not used.
faq.q3: What is sent to the server?
faq.a3: The book is read in your browser and turned into a single HTML page without scripts; only that page is sent to be printed as a PDF. On the server it is cleaned again, it can't load anything from the internet and it isn't stored: it's deleted when done.
faq.a4: The assembled page (with its images) can be up to 15 MB on the free plan and 50 MB with Pro. If your book has many images and goes over the limit, untick "Include the book's images".
faq.a4NoPro: The assembled page (with its images) can be up to 15 MB. If your book has many images and goes over the limit, untick "Include the book's images".

create-epub.title: Create EPUB
create-epub.description: Turn Markdown or HTML into an EPUB book with a table of contents, chapters and images, ready for any reader. In your browser.
create-epub.about: Turn your Markdown or HTML texts into an EPUB 3 ebook that opens in Apple Books, Google Play Books, Kobo, Calibre and almost any reader. Each file is a chapter, in the order of the list, and within each one a new chapter starts at every main heading (# in Markdown, h1 in HTML). The table of contents is generated, images embedded in the file are included, and you can set the title, author and language. Everything happens in your browser.

faq.q1: How are chapters split?
faq.a1: Each file starts a chapter, in the order of the list, and within each file a new chapter starts at every main heading (# in Markdown or h1 in HTML). The table of contents is built from those headings.
faq.q2: What about images?
faq.a2: Images embedded in the file itself (data URLs in PNG, JPG, GIF or WEBP) are included in the book. Images linked to the internet or to other files can't be downloaded and are replaced by their alternative text.
faq.q3: Does it work on Kindle?
faq.a3: Current Kindles accept EPUB through Amazon's "Send to Kindle", which converts it to their format. The file follows the EPUB 3 standard and also includes the EPUB 2 table of contents for older readers.
faq.a4: Yes. The content is cleaned: scripts, event handlers, forms and javascript: links are removed. Your files aren't uploaded to any server.

audio-converter.title: Audio Converter
audio-converter.description: Convert audio between MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A and AIFF in your browser, without uploading your files.
audio-converter.about: Convert songs, voice notes, podcasts and recordings between the most used formats: MP3 to play anywhere, lossless WAV, FLAC or AIFF to edit or archive, OGG (Opus) for the web and M4A (AAC) for Apple devices. Reads MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, Opus, M4A, AAC, WebM and AIFF, and you can choose the quality. The conversion happens on your device: files aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Which format should I pick?
faq.a1: MP3 if it must play on any device; M4A (AAC) sounds a bit better at the same size and is Apple's format; OGG (Opus) is the most efficient for the web; WAV and FLAC keep full quality (FLAC takes about half the space of WAV).
faq.q2: Does converting lose quality?
faq.a2: To WAV or FLAC, no: the sound is kept as is (in 16 bits). MP3, M4A and OGG are lossy: 192 kbps is practically indistinguishable from the original for most people; converting from one lossy format to another doesn't bring back what was already lost.
faq.q3: Why can't it read my M4A file?
faq.a3: AAC audio (M4A) is decoded with the browser's codec. Chrome, Edge and Safari read it; some browsers without proprietary codecs don't. In that case you'll see a notice: try another browser.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per file on the free plan (500 MB with Pro) and 3 hours long, because the result is built in your browser's memory. Only the main audio track is kept; if the file is a video, the picture is ignored.
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per file and 3 hours long, because the result is built in your browser's memory. Only the main audio track is kept; if the file is a video, the picture is ignored.
faq.q5: What is AIFF and when should I use it?
faq.a5: AIFF is Apple's lossless format, the Mac counterpart of WAV used by Logic or GarageBand. Uncompressed AIFF and AIFF-C (8, 16, 24 and 32-bit) are read and AIFF is written in 16 bits; compressed AIFF-C files (μ-law, for example) aren't supported.

trim-audio.title: Trim audio
trim-audio.description: Cut a section of a song or recording (MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A, AIFF) in your browser, with optional fades.
trim-audio.about: Keep only the part you need from a song, a voice message, a podcast or a recording: pick the start and end by typing minutes and seconds or with the player ("Use current position"), add a fade in or fade out if you like, and download the result as MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A or AIFF. The cut is sample-accurate and happens on your device: the file isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: How do I pick the exact section?
faq.a1: Play the audio, pause where you want it to begin and press "Use current position" next to Start; do the same for End. You can also type the times as minutes:seconds with tenths, for example 0:12.5 or 1:05.
faq.q2: What are the fades for?
faq.a2: The fade in raises the volume from silence over the first 2 seconds and the fade out lowers it to silence over the last 2, so the clip doesn't start or stop abruptly (handy for ringtones). On short clips each fade takes at most half of it.
faq.q3: Does it lose quality?
faq.a3: With WAV, FLAC or AIFF, no: the clip is saved losslessly (in 16 bits). MP3, M4A and OGG are compressed again at the quality you choose; 192 kbps is practically indistinguishable from the original.
faq.a4: One file at a time, up to 200 MB on the free plan (500 MB with Pro) and 3 hours long. It reads the same formats as "Audio converter"; M4A/AAC depends on your browser having that decoder.
faq.a4NoPro: One file at a time, up to 200 MB and 3 hours long. It reads the same formats as "Audio converter"; M4A/AAC depends on your browser having that decoder.

adjust-audio.title: Adjust audio
adjust-audio.description: Change the channels (mono or stereo), sample rate and bitrate of your audio files in the browser, in batches.
adjust-audio.about: Get audio ready for where it's going: turn a recording into mono so it takes half the space, lower the sample rate to 22.05 kHz for voice notes, take it to 48 kHz for video, or pick the exact bitrate a platform asks for. It works on several files at once and saves as MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG (Opus), M4A (AAC) or AIFF. Everything runs on your device: files aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: When should I switch to mono?
faq.a1: For speech (podcasts, lectures, interviews) stereo adds almost nothing: in mono the file is half the size at the same quality. Both channels are mixed together, so nothing that plays on one side only is lost.
faq.q2: Which sample rate should I choose?
faq.a2: 44.1 kHz is the music and CD rate; 48 kHz is the video rate; 22.05 kHz is enough for speech and reduces the size. Raising the rate doesn't add quality. OGG (Opus) always works at 48 kHz.
faq.q3: What bitrate do I need?
faq.a3: For speech, 64–96 kbps in mono; for music, 192 kbps or more. A higher bitrate sounds better and makes a bigger file. WAV, FLAC and AIFF have no bitrate because they're lossless.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per file on the free plan (500 MB with Pro), 3 hours per file and several files per batch. It reads the same formats as "Audio converter".
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per file, 3 hours per file and several files per batch. It reads the same formats as "Audio converter".

normalize-audio.title: Normalize volume
normalize-audio.description: Even out the volume of your audio files (MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A, AIFF) in the browser, by average loudness or peak, without clipping.
normalize-audio.about: Make a recording that came out too quiet louder, or match several tracks so they sound alike: the tool measures each whole file and applies one gain, so the dynamics don't change and there are no jumps. Choose average loudness (−16 dB, comfortable for voice and podcasts) or peak level (−1 dB). It never clips the peaks. It works in batches and on your device: files aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: What's the difference between average loudness and peak?
faq.a1: Peak only looks at the loudest point and puts it at −1 dB: it's safe, but two files can still sound different. Average loudness evens out how each file sounds (−16 dB RMS); if reaching it would push the peak over −1 dB, it stops at that limit.
faq.q2: Does it distort the sound?
faq.a2: No: one gain is applied to the whole file and −1 dB is never exceeded, so nothing clips. It isn't a compressor: a part much louder than the rest stays that way.
faq.q3: Why did my audio barely change?
faq.a3: If its peak is already near −1 dB or its average near −16 dB, the gain needed is small. The applied gain is shown next to each result. To avoid boosting noise, the largest increase is +30 dB.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per file on the free plan (500 MB with Pro), 3 hours per file and several files per batch. Each file is read twice (measure, then apply), so it takes a little longer than a conversion.
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per file, 3 hours per file and several files per batch. Each file is read twice (measure, then apply), so it takes a little longer than a conversion.

join-audio.title: Join audio
join-audio.description: Join several audio files (MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A, AIFF) into one, in the order you choose, in your browser.
join-audio.about: Put songs, parts of a recording, voice messages or podcast segments together into a single file: order them with the arrows, add a silence between tracks if you like, and download the result as MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A or AIFF. You can mix different formats: each file is decoded and matched in sample rate and channels before joining. Everything happens on your device: files aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Can I join files in different formats?
faq.a1: Yes: for example an MP3, a WAV and an M4A. Each one is decoded and brought to the same sample rate and channel count (the highest among them, at most stereo) before being joined in the format you choose.
faq.q2: How do I change the order?
faq.a2: Files are joined in the order of the list. Use the arrows on each row to move it up or down; the number on the left shows its position.
faq.q3: Is there a break between tracks?
faq.a3: No pauses are added unless you choose a silence between tracks (0.5, 1 or 2 seconds). Tracks are chained sample by sample; if a song ends abruptly, the change will be as noticeable as in the original.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per file on the free plan (500 MB with Pro) and 3 hours in total, because the result is built in your browser's memory. If a file is damaged, you're told which one.
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per file and 3 hours in total, because the result is built in your browser's memory. If a file is damaged, you're told which one.

video-converter.title: Video Converter
video-converter.description: Convert videos between MP4, MOV, MKV and WebM in your browser, without uploading your files.
video-converter.about: Change the format of your videos between MP4 (the one every phone, TV and social network plays), MOV (iPhone and Mac), MKV and WebM (the web's format). If the video already uses a codec the chosen format accepts, it is copied without re-encoding: it takes seconds and loses no quality. Otherwise it is re-encoded at high quality with your browser's codec. The sound goes along with the picture. Everything happens on your device: videos aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Does converting lose quality?
faq.a1: If only the container changes (for example, an H.264 MP4 to MOV or MKV), no: it is copied as is. If it must be re-encoded (for example, to WebM), a high quality is used that in practice can't be told apart from the original. Each result says whether it was copied or re-encoded.
faq.q2: Which format should I pick?
faq.a2: MP4 if it must play anywhere; MOV to edit in iMovie or Final Cut; WebM for a web page; MKV to keep everything as it is.
faq.q3: Why did my MP4 come out in VP9 or AV1?
faq.a3: Some browsers (such as Chromium or Firefox on Linux) have no H.264 encoder. Then the MP4 is made with VP9 or AV1, which play in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Android but maybe not on iPhone. For H.264 use Chrome, Edge or Safari; you'll see a notice when it's missing.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per file on the free plan (500 MB with Pro) and 2 hours long, because the video is built in your browser's memory. The main video and audio tracks are kept; embedded subtitles aren't copied. AVI, WMV and FLV can't be read yet.
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per file and 2 hours long, because the video is built in your browser's memory. The main video and audio tracks are kept; embedded subtitles aren't copied. AVI, WMV and FLV can't be read yet.

extract-audio.title: Extract Audio from Video
extract-audio.description: Take the sound out of an MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM video and save it as M4A, MP3, WAV, FLAC or OGG, in your browser.
extract-audio.about: Keep only the sound of a video: the music of a clip, the talk of a recorded class or the audio of a WhatsApp video. With “Original” the track is copied as it is, without re-encoding: it takes seconds and keeps the exact quality (a phone video gives an M4A with AAC). If you prefer another format, pick MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG (Opus), M4A (AAC) or AIFF and the quality. It accepts MP4, MOV, MKV and WebM, several at once. Everything happens on your device: videos aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Which format should I pick?
faq.a1: “Original” is the fastest and loses nothing: the audio keeps the format it already had inside the video (almost always AAC, in an .m4a file that iPhone, Android, Windows and Mac open). Pick MP3 for maximum compatibility, or WAV/FLAC to edit it.
faq.q2: Why did my file come out as MP3 with “Original”?
faq.a2: Some audio codecs have no format of their own to be copied into as they are (for example, the AC-3 of some films). Then it is converted to 192 kbps MP3 and the result says so.
faq.q3: Can I extract the audio of a YouTube video?
faq.a3: Only from files you already have on your device and have the right to use. This tool doesn't download videos from the internet.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per video on the free plan (500 MB with Pro) and 3 hours of audio. The main audio track is extracted. Converting the AAC audio of an MP4 to another format needs a browser that reads AAC (Chrome, Edge or Safari); “Original” works in all of them.
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per video and 3 hours of audio. The main audio track is extracted. Converting the AAC audio of an MP4 to another format needs a browser that reads AAC (Chrome, Edge or Safari); “Original” works in all of them.

compress-video.title: Compress Video
compress-video.description: Make your MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM videos smaller by lowering their quality or resolution, in your browser.
compress-video.about: Shrink videos to send them on WhatsApp or by email, upload them to a form or free up space on your phone. Choose the quality (high, medium or low) and, if you want, a lower resolution: taking a 1080p video down to 720p usually cuts the size a lot without showing on a phone screen. Vertical videos are handled too. The result comes out as MP4 (the most compatible) or WebM and we show how much smaller it got. Everything happens on your device: videos aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Which options should I choose?
faq.a1: For messaging, medium quality and 720p is a good balance. If it's still too big, try low quality or 480p. To keep the details, high quality and the original resolution.
faq.q2: Why does the size barely drop sometimes?
faq.a2: If the video was already heavily compressed (for example, downloaded from a social network), compressing it again saves little. Then the result says it didn't get smaller: lower the resolution to save more.
faq.q3: How long does it take?
faq.a3: Every frame is decoded and encoded again with your browser's codec: on a computer it's usually faster than the video's length; on older phones it can take longer. You can cancel at any time.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per video on the free plan (500 MB with Pro), 2 hours long and 30 minutes of processing per file. The picture is never enlarged. MP4 is made with H.264 when the browser allows it (Chrome, Edge, Safari); otherwise with VP9 or AV1.
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per video, 2 hours long and 30 minutes of processing per file. The picture is never enlarged. MP4 is made with H.264 when the browser allows it (Chrome, Edge, Safari); otherwise with VP9 or AV1.

trim-video.title: Trim Video
trim-video.description: Cut an MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM video and keep the part you want, in your browser.
trim-video.about: Keep only the moment that matters: the goal, the greeting or a part of a recorded meeting. Play the video, mark the start and end with “Use current position” (or type the times) and download the clip in the same format. Exact mode cuts at the precise frame by re-encoding the video; fast mode copies without re-encoding, in seconds and losslessly, starting at the key frame before the start. Everything happens on your device: the video isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: What's the difference between exact and fast?
faq.a1: Exact starts right where you marked, but it has to re-encode the video (it takes longer and compresses again at high quality). Fast copies the video as it is, so it takes seconds and loses nothing, but it can only start at a key frame: the result may begin up to a few seconds earlier.
faq.q2: How do I find the right moment?
faq.a2: Play the video and pause where you want; “Use current position” copies that time into the field. You can also type minutes:seconds, for example 1:23.5.
faq.q3: Can I remove a part in the middle?
faq.a3: For now one clip is kept at a time. To remove something in the middle, trim both parts and join them with “Join videos”.
faq.a4: One video at a time, up to 200 MB on the free plan (500 MB with Pro) and 2 hours long. If your browser can't play the file (for example MKV or H.264 in some), you can still type the times.
faq.a4NoPro: One video at a time, up to 200 MB and 2 hours long. If your browser can't play the file (for example MKV or H.264 in some), you can still type the times.

video-to-gif.title: Video to GIF
video-to-gif.description: Turn a part of an MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM video into an animated GIF, in your browser.
video-to-gif.about: Turn a moment of a video into an animated GIF for chats, forums, presentations or documentation. Mark the start and end with the player, choose the width (240 to 640 px) and the frames per second, and decide whether it repeats forever. Each frame gets its own 256-color palette so it looks as good as possible. Everything happens on your device: the video isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Why is the GIF so big?
faq.a1: GIF is an old format that stores each frame almost as a separate image. To make it smaller: shorten the clip, lower the width (320 px is enough for a chat) or use 5–10 frames per second.
faq.q2: How long can it be?
faq.a2: Up to 300 frames: 30 s at 10 frames per second, 20 s at 15 or 60 s at 5. If you go over, we tell you before starting.
faq.q3: Does it have sound?
faq.a3: No: the GIF format has no sound. If you need the audio, use “Trim video” and share the video.
faq.a4: One video at a time, up to 200 MB on the free plan (500 MB with Pro). The browser has to be able to decode the video (H.264 isn't decoded in some browsers without proprietary codecs). The picture is never enlarged.
faq.a4NoPro: One video at a time, up to 200 MB. The browser has to be able to decode the video (H.264 isn't decoded in some browsers without proprietary codecs). The picture is never enlarged.

video-speed.title: Change video speed
video-speed.description: Speed up or slow down an MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM video (0.25× to 4×), in your browser.
video-speed.about: Speed up a long tutorial, a screen recording or a time-lapse, or slow down a play or a funny moment. Pick a speed between 0.25× and 4× and decide whether to keep the sound (sped up or slowed down, higher or lower in pitch, like a tape) or remove it. The result downloads in the same format as the original, and you can process several videos at once. Everything happens on your device: the video isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: What happens to the sound?
faq.a1: If you keep it, it speeds up or slows down with the picture, so its pitch changes: at 2× voices sound higher and at 0.5× lower. If you'd rather have a silent video (to add music later, for example), choose “Remove sound”.
faq.q2: Is the slow motion smooth?
faq.a2: Each frame is shown for longer, so at 0.25× a 30 frames-per-second video plays at about 7.5. For smooth slow motion, record at 60 frames per second or more. When speeding up, extra frames are dropped so the result stays at 60 per second at most.
faq.q3: Is quality lost?
faq.a3: The video is re-encoded at high quality, in the same format as the original (MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM). The resolution doesn't change.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per video on the free plan (500 MB with Pro), 2 hours long and 30 minutes of processing per file. Your browser has to be able to decode the video (H.264 isn't decoded in some browsers without proprietary codecs).
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per video, 2 hours long and 30 minutes of processing per file. Your browser has to be able to decode the video (H.264 isn't decoded in some browsers without proprietary codecs).

join-videos.title: Join videos
join-videos.description: Join several MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM videos into one, in the order you choose, in your browser.
join-videos.about: Put the clips of a trip, the parts of a recorded class or several phone takes together into a single video. Add the files, put them in order with the arrows and download the result as MP4 or WebM. The final video takes the size of the first one: clips with another shape (vertical next to horizontal, for example) are fitted with black bands, never stretched or cropped. The sound of all of them is matched and, if a clip has no sound, that part stays silent. Everything happens on your device: the videos aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Can I join videos of different formats or sizes?
faq.a1: Yes: you can mix MP4, MOV, MKV and WebM, and horizontal and vertical videos. The result has the size of the first one in the list (1080p at most) and the others are centred with black bands.
faq.q2: How do I change the order?
faq.a2: The videos are joined in the order of the list. Use each file's arrows to move it up or down before joining.
faq.q3: Is quality lost?
faq.a3: The whole video is re-encoded at high quality so the parts fit together. Clips larger than the first one are scaled down to its size.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB per video on the free plan (500 MB with Pro), 2 hours in total and 30 minutes of processing. The result is built in your device's memory, so on phones it's best to join short videos. Your browser has to be able to decode each video (H.264 isn't decoded in some browsers without proprietary codecs).
faq.a4NoPro: Up to 200 MB per video, 2 hours in total and 30 minutes of processing. The result is built in your device's memory, so on phones it's best to join short videos. Your browser has to be able to decode each video (H.264 isn't decoded in some browsers without proprietary codecs).

model-converter.title: 3D model converter
model-converter.description: Convert 3D models (STL, OBJ, PLY, GLB, glTF, 3MF, COLLADA and FBX) to STL, OBJ, PLY or GLB in your browser, with nothing to install.
model-converter.about: Move a model from one format to another to 3D print it, open it in other software or publish it on the web: STL for printers and slicers, OBJ and PLY for editors and scanners, and GLB (binary glTF) for the web, augmented reality and game engines. It reads STL (binary and ASCII), OBJ, PLY, GLB, self-contained glTF, 3MF, COLLADA (.dae) and FBX 7.x (binary and ASCII), and keeps the geometry, where each part sits and, when the output format supports them (PLY and GLB), the vertex colors. You can convert several files at once. Everything happens on your device: the models aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Are materials and textures kept?
faq.a1: The shape is kept and, in PLY and GLB, the vertex colors. STL stores no colors or materials, and the OBJ is written without an .mtl file, so textures and materials are lost in those outputs. From GLB to GLB the materials are kept.
faq.q2: Does the size or orientation of the model change?
faq.a2: No: coordinates are copied as they are, without scaling or rotating. Note that many printing programs use Z as up while glTF uses Y, so after STL → GLB the model may appear lying down; rotate it in your viewer if needed.
faq.q3: My .gltf fails because of separate files. What can I do?
faq.a3: A .gltf can depend on a .bin and external images, which we can't fetch. Export it as GLB (a single file) or as glTF with everything embedded. glTF compressed with Draco or meshopt can't be read yet.
faq.a4: Up to 200 MB and 3 million triangles per model, and 5 minutes of processing per file. Point clouds (PLY without faces) can't be converted to meshes.
faq.q5: Can I convert 3MF, COLLADA or FBX files?
faq.a5: Yes, as input files: their geometry, parts and positions (and the vertex colors of COLLADA and FBX) are read and saved as STL, OBJ, PLY or GLB. No 3MF, COLLADA or FBX files are written, and their textures and animations aren't read. 3MF and COLLADA files can hold up to 100 MB of XML (uncompressed), and FBX files must be version 7.0 or later.

image-to-lithophane.title: Image to lithophane
image-to-lithophane.description: Turn a photo into a 3D lithophane (STL) ready to print, in your browser.
image-to-lithophane.about: A lithophane is a thin plate that shows a photo when light shines through it: dark areas are thicker and let less light pass. Upload a picture, choose the plate width, the level of detail and the thickness, and download a closed (watertight) STL ready for your 3D printer's slicer. You can add a frame for stiffness. Everything happens on your device: the photo isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: How do I print it?
faq.a1: Lay it flat side down on the bed, use white filament (white PLA is the usual choice), 100% infill and a layer height of 0.1–0.15 mm. Light it from behind to see the photo; it reads correctly from the relief side.
faq.q2: Which photos work best?
faq.a2: Ones with good contrast and a large subject: portraits, pets, landscapes with sky. Very light areas end up almost transparent and very dark ones opaque. The photo is turned to grayscale.
faq.q3: What do detail and thickness mean?
faq.a3: Detail is the distance between points of the surface: 0.4 mm is enough for a 0.4 mm nozzle and makes lighter files; 0.2 mm keeps more detail. Thickness goes from white (thinnest) to black (thickest): a larger range gives more contrast but needs more light.
faq.a4: One image at a time, up to 50 MB (JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF, BMP or AVIF). The surface has about 560,000 points at most: for very tall pictures the detail is reduced automatically. The plate is flat (not curved).

dxf-converter.title: DXF converter
dxf-converter.description: Convert DXF drawings from AutoCAD, LibreCAD or QCAD to SVG, PNG or PDF in your browser, with nothing to install.
dxf-converter.about: Turn a DXF drawing into an SVG to edit it in Inkscape or Illustrator or send it to a laser or vinyl cutter, a PNG to view or share it as a picture, or a PDF (A4 or A3) to print it. It draws lines, polylines (curved segments too), circles, arcs, ellipses, splines, solids, points, single-line and multiline texts, inserted blocks (with scale, rotation and arrays) and dimensions, in each entity's or layer's color. Layers that are off or frozen aren't drawn. When the file states its units (mm, cm, m or inches), the SVG has the real size. Everything happens on your device: the drawings aren't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Which entities aren't drawn?
faq.a1: Hatches (HATCH), embedded images, regions and 3D solids, multileaders, tables and block attributes. If the drawing has any, we tell you which ones and how many were left out when it's done. Only model space is drawn, not layouts (paper space).
faq.q2: Can I convert DWG files?
faq.a2: No. DWG is a closed Autodesk format and the engines that read it are GPL (LibreDWG) or commercial (ODA), so we can't include them. From AutoCAD, BricsCAD, DraftSight, LibreCAD or the free ODA File Converter you can save the drawing as DXF and convert it here.
faq.q3: Is the scale kept?
faq.a3: Yes: coordinates are copied unchanged and, when the DXF states its units ($INSUNITS in mm, cm, m or inches), the SVG is written at that real size, ready to print or cut 1:1. Without units, the longest side is 1000 pixels. Lines are thin and uniform (the file's lineweights aren't read).
faq.q4: Why do texts use a different font?
faq.a4: AutoCAD SHX fonts can't be embedded: texts are written in a sans-serif font (Arial or similar) at the same height, so their width may differ slightly. The usual MTEXT formatting codes are understood (paragraphs, Ø, °, ±).
faq.a5: Up to 50 MB per file (text DXF; binary DXF isn't read), 5 million points once curves are drawn, blocks nested up to 16 levels and arrays of up to 10,000 copies, and 2 minutes of processing per file.
faq.q6: What do the PNG and the PDF look like?
faq.a6: The PNG has the width you choose (1000, 2000 or 4000 pixels on the longest side), with a white or transparent background. The PDF is vector, one A4 or A3 page turned to match the drawing's shape, with the drawing fitted inside a 10 mm margin (not at 1:1 scale). In the PDF, texts with characters the standard font lacks (Chinese, Cyrillic…) are inserted as images.

text-to-speech.title: Text to speech
text-to-speech.description: Paste text or open a file and listen to it with pause and the speed you choose, or download it as MP3 with an AI voice, in your browser.
text-to-speech.searchTerms: TTS read aloud reader narrator voice reader speech synthesis AI voice
text-to-speech.about: Type or paste text, or open a TXT, Markdown, HTML, text PDF, Word (DOCX) or EPUB file or a photo of a document, and listen to it read aloud. You can pause, go back to the previous sentence, skip to the next one and choose the speed, from 0.5× to 2×. The sentence being read is highlighted so you can follow along. It reads with your device's voices or with a more natural AI voice (Supertonic 3) that runs in your browser and lets you download the reading as MP3. The text is extracted and turned into speech on your device: the file is never uploaded to a server.

faq.q1: Is my text uploaded to a server?
faq.a1: No. The file is read and its text extracted in your browser, and the AI voice generates the audio on your device: the only download is the model files, from Hugging Face, the first time. Device voices also read on your computer or phone; only voices marked "online" (such as Google or Microsoft voices in Chrome and Edge) send the text to that provider to generate the audio.
faq.q2: Which files can I open?
faq.a2: TXT, Markdown, HTML, PDFs with text, Word (DOCX), EPUB and photos or scans (JPG, PNG, WEBP, TIFF, HEIC…), whose text is recognized with OCR. Up to 50,000 characters per reading; longer text is cut and we tell you.
faq.q3: Which languages does it read?
faq.a3: We detect the language of the text (Spanish, English, Portuguese, French or Chinese) and pick a voice for it; you can change the language and the voice. The AI voice and MP3 download are available in Spanish, English, Portuguese and French; Chinese is read with the device voices, which depend on your system and browser.
faq.q4: What's the difference between device voices and the AI voice?
faq.a4: Device voices come with your system or browser: they start at once and download nothing, but their quality varies and they can't be saved as a file. The AI voice (Supertonic 3) sounds more natural, has 10 voices and can be downloaded as MP3, but the first time it downloads about 400 MB (then it stays saved in your browser) and it generates the audio with your device's processor: on a computer it takes about as long as the audio lasts; on a phone, quite a bit longer.
faq.q5: How do I download the reading as MP3?
faq.a5: Choose the AI voice and press "Download MP3". It is generated sentence by sentence on your device, with a progress bar and a cancel button, and the file is named after the document's title or the first words of the text. On phones the MP3 can have up to 3,000 characters (about 4 minutes of audio).
faq.q6: Can I publish audio made with the AI voice?
faq.a6: Yes, but the model's license (OpenRAIL-M) requires saying that it is an AI-generated voice and forbids using it to, among other things, impersonate people, defame, harass or spread false information to harm others. The full restrictions are in our Terms and in the model's license, linked next to the download button.
